name: Manifests and media QA
observations: OpenMontage defines JSON Schema contracts for asset manifests, render reports, source-media reviews, character QA reports, pipeline manifests, and checkpoints. The asset manifest requires version 1.0 and per-asset id/type/path/source_tool/scene_id, while allowing provenance, cost, duration, resolution, format, quality score, license, provider, and narration-review metadata (schemas/artifacts/asset_manifest.schema.json:2-61).

The render-report schema requires at least one output and per-output path, format, resolution, and duration; it also models codec/audio codec/fps/file size, warnings, verification notes, renderer family, slideshow risk, decision-log linkage, and final-review linkage (schemas/artifacts/render_report.schema.json:2-62).

The source-media-review schema explicitly permits an empty files array for fully generated productions, but requires a summary and at least one planning implication; reviewed files must be marked reviewed=true and can carry technical probe data, content/transcript summaries, representative frames, quality risks, and usability (schemas/artifacts/source_media_review.schema.json:4-82).

The character QA report models pass/revise/fail status and checks for schema validity, asset existence, pivots, poses, timing, motion, browser preview, and frame samples, plus issues and a recommended action (schemas/artifacts/character_qa_report.schema.json:4-33).

Pipeline manifests are declarative and schema-validated. They define ordered stages, required/optional input artifacts, produced artifacts, tools, review focus, success criteria, checkpoint and human-approval defaults, conditional sub-stages, reference-input support, orchestration limits, and extension permissions (schemas/pipelines/pipeline_manifest.schema.json:4-195).

Checkpoint validation maps canonical stages to canonical artifacts, treats source_media_review/final_review/video_analysis_brief as governance supplements, rejects invalid stages/statuses/artifact containers, validates known artifact payloads against JSON Schema, and requires the canonical artifact for completed or awaiting_human stages (lib/checkpoint.py:30-48, 124-191).

Pipeline YAML is loaded with safe_load and validated against the pipeline-manifest schema; stage order, sub-stage activation, required tools, review focus, human approval defaults, and extension permissions are exposed through helper functions (lib/pipeline_loader.py:49-70, 98-182, 201-239).

Source-media review detects media by extension, skips unknown or missing files, probes video/audio through registered tools with ffprobe fallback, samples four video timestamps into per-file directories, performs optional transcription, derives low-resolution/mono/short-clip risks, and emits planning implications (lib/source_media_review.py:23-38, 41-136, 139-206, 209-350).

OpenMontage’s video compose final review is explicitly a governance contract: it must inspect the actual output using ffprobe and frame sampling before compose completion (tools/video/video_compose.py:2289-2310). It records container validity, duration, resolution, fps, audio presence, codec, and file size, flags short/duration-drift/low-resolution/no-audio conditions, samples four frames, checks black frames, analyzes volume/clipping, checks runtime swaps and delivery promises, checks subtitle presence, and compares transcript to script (tools/video/video_compose.py:2315-2653). Invalid containers force fail/re-render; other issues may produce pass or revise with a recommended action (tools/video/video_compose.py:2655-2700).

OpenMontage’s opt-in HyperFrames QA exercises scaffold, lint, browser validation/contrast reporting, and optionally a real render; the full-render branch probes the resulting MP4 with ffprobe and requires a valid video stream and nontrivial file size (tests/qa/test_09_hyperframes_compose.py:1-15, 106-189). The synthetic end-to-end QA walks stages, validates artifacts/checkpoints/cost tracking, and uses ffmpeg-generated fixtures for a real compose output (tests/qa/test_08_end_to_end.py:1-9, 22-31, 58-79).

Backlot visual QA stages projects, captures fixed browser screenshots, compares changed-pixel ratio against goldens with configurable masks and a 1.5% default threshold, writes red diffs and report.json, and optionally runs Playwright interaction smoke tests (scripts/backlot_visual_eval.py:1-10, 35-86, 149-163, 166-230).

Atlas media smoke is explicitly opt-in and refuses paid calls without --allow-paid. It checkpoints successful records to smoke_manifest.json, preserves prior successes for resumability, records provider/model/cost/artifacts/data/error, and exits nonzero unless all configured image/video cases succeed (scripts/atlas_media_smoke.py:152-184, 186-233).

MPS has an independently written ProductionManifest dataclass with version, pipeline, render runtime, storyboard, provider order/decisions, required tools, quality-gate names, outputs, and warnings; its declared gates include storyboard validation, 16:9, 15-45 seconds, playable H.264, representative-frame inspection, and mastery-check presence (MPS-git/scripts/production_manifest.py:19-73).

MPS’s render manifest is generated from RenderResult.to_dict and records provider, output path, requested duration/aspect ratio, audio boolean, fallback assets, errors, and a list of quality-gate strings; the checked-in example contains no codec, resolution, file-size, fps, probe, frame-sample, or gate-result fields (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:35-56, 247-250; MPS-git/build/mpve-demo/jobs/mps-6e32d626700b/render.manifest.json:1-14).

MPS’s local renderer validates the storyboard and requires ffmpeg, then encodes H.264 at fixed 1280x720/24 fps, but returns quality-gate labels rather than independently probing the produced file; the hybrid path falls back to hosted output or SVG assets and reports the selected provider (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:183-210, 216-250).

MPS MPVE marks a job completed when result.output_path exists, without validating the generated artifact against a media schema or running ffprobe/frame/audio QA in the completion path (MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:196-228). The unit-test fake renderer writes bytes that are explicitly not a real video, yet the success test expects completed state and an artifact path (MPS-git/tests/test_mpve.py:23-26, 49-63).
inferences: OpenMontage treats manifests as cross-stage contracts and QA reports as durable governance artifacts, not merely diagnostic logs; checkpoint persistence is the enforcement boundary.

OpenMontage separates technical validation, visual spot-checking, audio validation, semantic transcript checks, delivery-promise checks, and human review status, allowing a render to be technically valid but still require revision.

OpenMontage’s source-media contract is designed to prevent planning from assuming content that was never inspected; its empty-review state makes fully generated production explicit rather than ambiguous.
MPS currently has the beginnings of an auditable provider/quality vocabulary, but its manifest is descriptive and renderer-centric rather than schema-backed and evidence-backed.
MPS can report a successful job for bytes that are not a decodable MP4 under the current mocked-success contract; this indicates a production correctness gap, not merely a test simplification.

The MPS fallback distinction is partly honest because provider, audio, fallback assets, and errors are recorded, but the manifest does not preserve enough probe evidence to establish what was actually delivered.
OpenMontage’s screenshot/golden QA is specific to its Backlot UI and should not be conflated with final media QA; MPS has no comparable deterministic visual regression layer for rendered MP4 frames.
unknowns: The inspected OpenMontage schemas do not by themselves prove that every producer writes every optional field or that every pipeline enforces every declared success_criteria item; producer/consumer coverage remains distributed across skills and tools.

The source-media reviewer’s transcription and frame-sampling behavior depends on tool availability; the artifact can remain structurally valid with absent optional transcript/frame data, so the minimum evidence policy for each media type is not fully specified by schema alone.

OpenMontage’s final-review status policy intentionally permits pass with non-critical issues; the precise human escalation policy is partly delegated to stage skills/reviewers rather than encoded as a universal schema rule.
MPS’s current hosted-provider hook and any future server/process-restart behavior are outside the manifest and media-QA files inspected here.
No MPS JSON Schema for production manifests, render manifests, or final media QA reports was found in the inspected repository paths.
contracts: A valid OpenMontage asset manifest is version 1.0, has an assets array, and each asset identifies its path, type, source tool, and scene association; paths are described as relative to the pipeline project (schemas/artifacts/asset_manifest.schema.json:7-23).

A valid OpenMontage render report has at least one output, and each output supplies path, format, resolution, and nonnegative duration; optional verification notes and final-review linkage provide audit context (schemas/artifacts/render_report.schema.json:7-28, 30-60).

A source-media review must not claim review without actual probing/sampling/transcription activity; unknown or nonexistent inputs are skipped, and no-source production is represented explicitly with a planning implication (lib/source_media_review.py:8-10, 247-250, 263-350).

Completed or awaiting-human canonical OpenMontage stages must carry their canonical artifact, and known artifact objects must pass their registered JSON Schema before checkpoint persistence (lib/checkpoint.py:124-191).

Pipeline stage order and gate defaults come from the validated pipeline manifest; callers should not infer stage order from unordered collections or ad hoc lists (lib/pipeline_loader.py:39-46, 125-149).

OpenMontage compose completion should be based on actual post-render review evidence, including a real media probe and frame sample; invalid containers must result in fail/re-render (tools/video/video_compose.py:2297-2310, 2675-2700).

Backlot visual regression passes only when changed pixels are at or below the configured threshold after declared masks; a diff image and JSON report are emitted (scripts/backlot_visual_eval.py:49-86, 149-163, 225-230).

MPS request validation requires topic/objective, 15-45 seconds, 16:9, consented-analogy constraints, and derived=true for FHP modes; those are planning/request contracts, not equivalent to output-media QA (MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:71-85).

MPS’s current completion contract is output-path existence plus renderer-returned metadata; it does not require a decodable output or schema-valid render report (MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:203-226).
mps_gaps: No schema-backed ProductionManifest/render.manifest contract: MPS serializes dataclasses and renderer results directly, so required fields, types, additional properties, and version migrations are not validated as a boundary.

No canonical asset-manifest artifact: generated/fallback assets are represented as a loose fallback_assets list and provider metadata, without per-asset scene association, source/license/provenance, cost, quality, or relative-path contract comparable to OpenMontage asset_manifest.

No source-media-review artifact or pre-planning inspection gate: MPS request/storyboard flow has no structured probe, representative-frame, transcript-summary, risk, or planning-implication record for user-supplied media.

No durable final_review artifact: MPS result payload exposes quality_gates and errors but does not persist technical probe, visual spot-check, audio spot-check, subtitle, transcript comparison, delivery-promise, status, or recommended-action evidence.

Quality gates are labels rather than independently evaluated results: local rendering returns strings such as H.264 encode and 16:9 dimensions without checking the actual file after encoding; hosted output only receives a provider-output-exists label; SVG fallback receives SVG-assets-generated (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:210,238,244).

MPVE completion is vulnerable to false positives because it checks only output_path.exists(); the existing fake-success test demonstrates that invalid bytes can satisfy the completion path (MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:206-226; MPS-git/tests/test_mpve.py:23-26,49-63).

No frame sampling, black-frame detection, audio-volume/clipping/silence analysis, subtitle-presence check, transcript-vs-script comparison, or runtime/delivery-promise preservation review is wired into MPVE completion.

No explicit distinction between requested/observed media properties in the render manifest: requested duration/aspect ratio can be recorded even if the encoded output differs, and codec/resolution/fps/file size are absent from the checked-in manifest.

No checkpoint/stage artifact protocol around MPVE jobs: job.json persists lifecycle state, but there is no canonical stage-to-artifact requirement, human gate state, or schema validation equivalent to OpenMontage checkpoint enforcement.

MPS tests cover request validation, idempotent deduplication, lifecycle, and exception propagation, but do not include a real or mocked ffprobe-negative test proving invalid media is rejected, nor a schema-invalid manifest test.
clean_room_recommendations: Define an independently authored versioned MPVE render-report schema with separate requested, observed, and verdict sections. Require output path, container validity, codec, dimensions, fps, duration, file size, audio presence, provider, fallback state, errors, and evidence paths; reject unknown fields or document an extension namespace.

Add a post-render validation step before setting completed: run ffprobe on the actual artifact, verify a video stream and expected aspect/duration bounds, and perform a full decode or equivalent decode smoke. Persist the probe result and gate verdict; do not infer validity from file existence.

Create a durable final-review object for MPVE with technical probe, representative frame paths, black/blank-frame checks, audio presence/level/silence checks, optional subtitle check, and a status/recommended-action field. Keep human taste review separate from deterministic checks.

Represent fallback outputs explicitly as different artifact kinds and enforce that a fallback-only run cannot claim a genuine MP4 artifact. Preserve provider decision rationale and all attempted-provider errors in the report.

Add a source-media review contract only if MPVE will accept user media; require actual probe evidence before planning and record actionable risks. If MPVE remains generated-only, state that limitation explicitly in its request/schema rather than silently omitting the concept.

Add schema validation and migration/version tests for production and render manifests, including required-field failures, unknown-field behavior, round-trip serialization, and backward compatibility policy.

Extend MPVE tests with a corrupt/non-video output, wrong codec, wrong dimensions, duration drift, missing audio when audio is expected, and truncated/decode-failure cases; assert failed state and persisted diagnostic evidence.

Make quality gates structured records with id, observed value, threshold, pass/fail, and evidence reference rather than free-form strings. Keep educational gates such as mastery-check presence distinct from media integrity gates.

Add representative-frame extraction to the successful local path and optionally deterministic frame-diff/golden tests for stable local renders; avoid making aesthetic judgments automatic unless the contract defines measurable checks.

Use an append-only or immutable job artifact bundle containing request fingerprint, storyboard, production manifest, render report, final review, and provider/fallback decisions so downstream MPS delivery can audit exactly what was generated.
